subject: Acumen Health - follow-up: SOC 2, data retention & deletion SLAs
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Farrell <jessica.farrell@acumenhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Acumen Health - follow-up: SOC 2, data retention & deletion SLAs

Hi Jessica —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the procurement timeline:

Summary of what we covered:
- Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in scope for our hosted API; SOC 2 summary and controls mapping shared below.
- You asked for clarification on data retention (application layer tokens vs. backups), deletion SLA for user-initiated requests, and log retention for troubleshooting/audit.
- HIPAA: Redwood supports Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for covered workloads; we discussed options for dedicated/private deployments.

Asks / next steps:
1) I will send our SOC 2 one-pager and a short mapping to the vendor questionnaire items you flagged (see attached).
2) Can your team confirm the retention window you must enforce for telemetry vs. customer content? We suggested a default: 30 days for request/response KV cache, 90 days for audit logs, backups retained for 180 days (encrypt-at-rest). Let me know if that aligns with your policy.
3) Procurement asked for deletion SLA language — proposal: "Customer-deletion requests completed within 5 business days for primary data; backups on a 180-day rotation with secure deletion procedures." Open to adjustments.

If you like, we can loop in Vanessa (security lead) to run through the vendor security questionnaire and provide the SOC 2 artifact set.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[attachment: SOC2_summary_redwood.pdf (application/pdf)]
From: Jessica Farrell <jessica.farrell@acumenhealth.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acumenhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acumen Health - follow-up: SOC 2, data retention & deletion SLAs

Connor —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifying points from our side:

- SOC 2: can you confirm the date of the latest Type II report and whether there are any scoped exclusions (we need to surface that to our InfoSec).
- Retention windows: Our baseline policy is 90 days for application content and telemetry, but we have a stricter rule for PHI-related metadata when a BAA is in place (30 days preferred). Can you confirm support for a 30-day option under BAA?
- Deletion SLA: 5 business days for primary data sounds OK; however backups must have certified destruction timelines or secure-wipe proof. Procurement needs concrete language.
- Vendor questionnaire: we'll start the intake and attach your responses into our procurement packet. Please send any artifacts you can now.

Also, can you provide a named contact for security ops for a short technical call this week?

Thanks,
Jessica Farrell
Director, IT Security | Acumen Health
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Farrell <jessica.farrell@acumenhealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acumen Health - follow-up: SOC 2, data retention & deletion SLAs

Jessica — thanks for the specific asks. Looping in Vanessa (Head of Security Ops) and Sean (solutions) to respond with artifacts and a recommended SLA paragraph you can copy into the contract.

Vanessa / Sean — can you confirm:
- latest SOC 2 Type II audit period end date, any scoped exclusions;
- support for a 30-day retention mode when a BAA is executed (we can disable backups retention of content in that mode or mark backups for expedited rotation for that customer);
- deletion SLA wording and certified backup destruction process (we keep manifest-level logs of deletes and can provide a Certificate of Destruction on request).

Suggested contract language (draft):
"Redwood will honor Customer requests to delete Customer Data within five (5) business days. Backups are retained for a maximum of one hundred eighty (180) days; upon verified deletion requests Redwood will schedule backup data for secure destruction and provide a Certificate of Destruction within thirty (30) calendar days of completion."

CC: Jessica — if that draft looks close we can attach it to the procurement packet and Vanessa can share the SOC 2 artifact bundle and the vendor questionnaire template.

Cheers,
Connor
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Farrell <jessica.farrell@acumenhealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acumen Health - follow-up: SOC 2, data retention & deletion SLAs

Hi Jessica —

Nice to meet you (virtually). A few concrete items from security:

1) SOC 2: Latest Type II report period ended 2026-06-30. No scoped exclusions for data storage or the hosted inference service. PDF attached.
2) BAA/PHI support: We support a 30-day retention profile for content under a BAA. In that mode we operate an accelerated backup rotation and will mark customer backups for expedited purge windows. Note backups may be immutable for a short window depending on cloud provider snapshot mechanics; we include that in the deletion certificate.
3) Deletion & backup destruction: We maintain deletion manifests and can provide a Certificate of Destruction once backup purge completes. Our internal SLA for completing backup purges after a verified deletion request is 30 calendar days; primary data deletions are completed within 5 business days.
4) Logs/audit retention: Standard audit logs retained for 90 days; long-term retention for legal hold requests can be extended by mutual agreement.

I've attached the fillable vendor security questionnaire and our SOC 2 summary. If you prefer, Sean can run a focused 30-minute technical call on Thursday to walk through questions about backup immutability and KMS/HSM controls.

Attachments:
- vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)
- SOC2_summary_redwood.pdf (PDF, 240KB)

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
